citations.text: Efklides, A., & Schwartz, B. L. (2024). Revisiting the Metacognitive and Affective Model of Self-Regulated Learning: Origins, Development, and Future Directions. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 61.

en.general: An unpleasant sense that working on a task is not going smoothly. It comes from the task and from the learner noticing the trouble, and the article says it has no particular action attached. What a student does next depends on what they blame it on.

examples: A student frowns and pauses because the plan for the flashlight does not work.
A student feels partway through that a problem is hard although she judged it easy at the start.
nonExamples: A student's estimate, before starting, of how demanding the task is.
Fear of failure that makes a student withdraw.
